Whose pipe is it?

The City of Wadsworth owns and runs a separate sanitary sewer system and its own wastewater treatment plant. The pipe from your house to that public sewer is a different matter. The city's Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook says maintaining and repairing a building service line is the building owner's job.

A camera inspection can show where the trouble sits before anyone starts cleaning. That keeps you from paying to clear a private line when the problem is in the street, or the other way around.

Report first, then call

The city's backup handbook asks residents to report a sanitary sewer backup to the city as soon as it happens and before calling a plumber.

Older houses, mixed pipe

Wadsworth was settled in 1814, and by 1863 a railroad ran through the south end of town. Coal mining was the largest business for nearly 50 years, and the early 1900s brought match, injector, salt and brick companies that drew workers to town (Main Street Wadsworth history).

Houses built for that workforce sit beside newer streets. The city handbook notes that many homes built before 1960 had foundation drains tied into the sanitary service, which can overload the sewer in heavy rain. Jetting cannot fix that, which is one more reason to look first.

From symptoms to a sensible next step.

  1. Describe the drain problem.Note which fixtures are slow, whether sewage has backed up and whether a past cleaning helped.
  2. Check the line.A qualified professional can locate the obstruction and judge whether the pipe can take jetting.
  3. Choose the work that fits.Buildup may clear with cleaning. A cracked joint or a collapsed section may need repair too.

severe-grease-and-sludge.title: Severe Grease and Sludge in Wadsworth, OH | Wadsworth Hydro Jetting Pros
severe-grease-and-sludge.desc: Grease and sludge in Wadsworth drain lines: why kitchen drains slow down and what to check before hydro jetting.
severe-grease-and-sludge.h1: Grease and sludge in Wadsworth kitchen and main lines
severe-grease-and-sludge.heroP: Grease cools and sticks to the walls of a drain, so a line can narrow for years before it finally stops.

sections.html:
Why grease keeps coming back

Hot grease runs freely down a kitchen drain and then cools in the first cold stretch of pipe. Layer after layer builds up on the pipe wall, and the sink may still drain, just more slowly each month. Plunging or a quick snake pass can open a hole through the middle without removing the coating.

Hydro jetting uses directed water to scrape that coating off suitable pipe. It works best when the pipe is sound and the nozzle fits the line.

Wadsworth buildings and old lines

The older blocks of Wadsworth's downtown were built in the late 1800s and early 1900s, and they now hold a mix of businesses and apartments (Downtown Wadsworth Historic District page). Kitchen lines in older buildings can include sections of different materials and ages, and some may have been patched over the decades.

Before cleaning a heavily greased line, a camera can show where the grease is thickest and whether the pipe wall is intact. Cleaning a weak section hard is a poor bet.

Keeping grease out of the sewer

The city's sewer system is separate from storm drains and is built to carry household wastewater to its treatment plant (Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook). Grease that hardens in a private line can still back up into a basement floor drain. Wipe pans before washing and keep fats out of the sink.

A good question to ask

Ask where the grease is building up and whether the pipe is sound enough to be jetted.

tree-root-intrusions.desc: Tree roots in Wadsworth, OH sewer service lines: what the city handbook says about owner responsibility and cleaning schedules.
tree-root-intrusions.h1: Tree roots in Wadsworth sewer service lines
tree-root-intrusions.heroP: Roots find the joints and hairline cracks in a buried pipe, and in Wadsworth the homeowner owns the line from the house to the public sewer.

sections.html:
Roots and who pays attention to them

The Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook says tree roots can tangle in a sewer line and cause a backup. It also says that maintenance and repair of an individual building service are the building owner's responsibility.

That makes root problems a private-line issue in most cases. A camera can show where roots enter and whether the pipe around them is still sound.

What the city handbook describes

The handbook says the line should first be cleaned with an electric rodding machine fitted with a root cutter. After that, some owners have the line cleaned on a regular schedule. It notes that some have needed this as often as every six months, while others need it only once every few years.

It also describes root-remover products as something that may lengthen the time between cleanings, and pipe replacement as the surest permanent fix. It suggests getting more than one opinion before deciding.

Where jetting fits

Water jetting can cut and flush some root growth from a line that is otherwise sound. It does not close the gap the roots came through. If a joint is open or a section is broken, repair may be needed.

recurring-clogs-and-slow-drains.title: Recurring Clogs and Slow Drains in Wadsworth, OH | Wadsworth Hydro Jetting Pros
recurring-clogs-and-slow-drains.desc: Recurring clogs and slow drains in Wadsworth, OH: private lines, the public main, and rain-related backups explained.
recurring-clogs-and-slow-drains.h1: Recurring clogs and slow drains in Wadsworth homes
recurring-clogs-and-slow-drains.heroP: When one drain keeps clogging, the answer is often not at the drain. It can be a partly blocked line, a main that fills in heavy rain, or both.

sections.html:
Three places a backup can start

The Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook lists three causes: a blockage in the private sewer lateral, a blockage in the public main, or an overloaded main during rainstorms. Only the first is the owner's to fix.

If a neighbor with a similar house did not back up and you did, the private line is a likelier suspect. If several neighbors are affected, the main may be the cause, and the city should hear about it.

Why age of house matters

The handbook says houses built before 1960 often had a foundation drain connected to the sanitary service, and that roof downspouts and area drains were sometimes connected too. Those connections send storm water into a system built for household wastewater, and the city says they violate its ordinances.

A hydro jetting visit cannot undo that. It can clear buildup that is making an already stressed line worse.

What to do when a drain keeps clogging

  1. Report a backup.Sewage in the basement should be reported to the city first, then to a qualified professional.
  2. Look at the line.A camera shows buildup, roots, offsets or standing water.
  3. Match the fix to the cause.Cleaning for buildup, repair for damage, and a conversation with the city if the main is involved.

mineral-and-scale-deposits.title: Mineral and Scale Deposits in Wadsworth, OH | Wadsworth Hydro Jetting Pros
mineral-and-scale-deposits.desc: Mineral and scale deposits in older Wadsworth, OH pipes: how they build, how to check, and when cleaning is not enough.
mineral-and-scale-deposits.h1: Mineral and scale deposits in older Wadsworth pipes
mineral-and-scale-deposits.heroP: Scale builds slowly on the inside of a pipe, so a drain can lose capacity over years without anyone noticing a single bad day.

sections.html:
How scale builds

Minerals in water can leave a hard crust inside a drain line, especially in older iron or galvanized pipe and at spots where flow slows. The pipe still carries water, but through a smaller opening. Each new bit of grease or paper then has less room to pass.

Because the change is slow, people often blame the last thing that went down the drain. A camera can show the real condition of the pipe wall.

Older homes and mixed materials

Wadsworth's population grew quickly in the early 1900s when match, injector, salt and brick plants opened, and many of those houses are still in use (Main Street Wadsworth history). Over a century, a house may have had pieces of its plumbing replaced while other pieces stayed.

A line of mixed materials can show scale in one stretch and clean plastic in the next. That is one reason to inspect before choosing a nozzle.

When cleaning is not enough

Hard scale can leave a pipe thin or pitted. If the camera shows a weak wall, repair may be the safer choice than pressure cleaning.

preventative-maintenance.title: Preventative Maintenance in Wadsworth, OH | Wadsworth Hydro Jetting Pros
preventative-maintenance.desc: Preventative drain care for Wadsworth, OH homes: regular cleaning, sump pump checks and keeping storm water out of the sewer.
preventative-maintenance.h1: Preventative drain care for Wadsworth homes
preventative-maintenance.heroP: A little attention to the private line, the sump pump and the floor drain can head off the kind of backup that ruins a basement.

sections.html:
What the city suggests

The Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook says some owners keep roots under control by having the line cleaned on a regular schedule. It also lists simple home checks for people who depend on a sump pump: pour water into it every month to make sure it runs and empties quickly, and clean the strainer on the suction side every six months.

These are small tasks that cost little time and tell you early if something has changed.

Keep storm water out of the sanitary line

The handbook says foundation drains, roof downspouts and sump pumps should not be connected to the sanitary sewer. In its words, those connections violate city ordinances and add to overloading during heavy rain.

If your house is older and has a basement but no sump pump, ask a qualified professional to trace where the foundation drain goes.

Know your line before you need it

Ask for a camera inspection when you buy a house or when drains slow down. A recording of the pipe today makes it easier to spot changes later.

Call 811 before you dig

The city's planning and zoning page reminds residents to call Ohio Utility Protection Service at 811 before any digging.

how-hydro-jetting-works.desc: How hydro jetting works: camera inspection, nozzle choice and cleaning steps for sewer and drain lines in Wadsworth, OH.
how-hydro-jetting-works.h1: How hydro jetting works in a Wadsworth sewer line
how-hydro-jetting-works.heroP: The method is simple to describe: a nozzle on a hose pushes water at high pressure through a pipe. What matters is whether your pipe is fit for it.

sections.html:
Inspection comes first

A camera on a flexible cable shows what is in the line and what shape the pipe is in. It can reveal grease, roots, scale, an offset joint or a collapsed section. That picture decides whether jetting makes sense.

Choosing the nozzle and the pressure

The nozzle is picked to suit the pipe and the material blocking it. Some nozzles send jets backward to pull the hose forward and scrape the wall, while others spin to cut at buildup. A fragile pipe should not get the same treatment as a sturdy one.

What happens in Wadsworth lines

Most homes here are on the city's sanitary sewer, and the owner is responsible for the line from the house to the public sewer (Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook). Work is done on that private line. If a camera suggests the main is blocked, the city should be told.

hydro-jetting-vs-snaking.desc: Hydro jetting vs snaking: how each method works on grease, roots and buildup in Wadsworth, OH drains.
hydro-jetting-vs-snaking.h1: Hydro jetting vs snaking for Wadsworth drains
hydro-jetting-vs-snaking.heroP: A snake bores through a clog. A jet washes the pipe wall. Which one fits depends on what is blocking the line.

sections.html:
What a snake does well

A cable machine can open a drain fast and is common for a simple blockage. The city's handbook describes electric rodding with a root cutter as the first step for roots in a service line (Wadsworth Sanitary Sewer Backup Handbook).

What a jet adds

Water jetting scours the inside of the pipe. That can remove grease and sludge that a cable only pokes a hole through. It is a poor fit for a broken pipe, because pressure can make a bad section worse.

How to decide

If the same drain keeps clogging after snaking, ask whether buildup is left behind. A camera can show what a cable missed and help match the tool to the pipe.

How Hydro Jetting WorksRecurring Clogs and Slow Drains

downtown-wadsworth.h1: Hydro jetting questions for downtown Wadsworth buildings
downtown-wadsworth.heroP: The Downtown Wadsworth Historic District sits on the National Register of Historic Places. Its buildings are old, and so is much of what runs beneath them.

sections.html:
A downtown that grew with the railroad

Judge Frederick Brown bought land two miles west of the first settlers in 1816, and the downtown later grew up at that spot (Main Street Wadsworth history). The railroad arrived in 1863, and the early 1900s brought several large companies and a surge of new residents.

Buildings from different decades now stand side by side, and their plumbing was added, moved and replaced as uses changed.

What historic listing does and does not do

The city's page says National Register listing recognizes a property's significance, does not restrict its use and does not require maintenance of private property (Downtown Wadsworth Historic District page). Drain work is therefore a normal repair question. An owner should still check with the right office before altering the exterior of a building or opening a street.

The City of Wadsworth permits page lists a sewer and street opening permit among its permit types, and the City of Wadsworth planning and zoning page says plumbing permits go through the Medina County Health Department.

Questions worth asking downtown

Older commercial and mixed-use buildings can share lines or have kitchens above and below one another. A camera inspection can show where a shared line runs and what condition it is in. For a basement backup, report it to the city first, then bring in a qualified professional.

wadsworth-township.desc: Hydro jetting questions for Wadsworth Township, OH: sewer or septic, county health department rules, soils and older coal-area homes.
wadsworth-township.h1: Hydro jetting questions for Wadsworth Township homes
wadsworth-township.heroP: Outside the city limits, a home may be on a public sewer or on its own septic system. That one fact changes every drain question.

sections.html:
Sewer or septic?

The Medina County Health Department permits and inspects new and replacement household sewage treatment systems in the county. It also says that if a property can reach a sanitary sewer, the house must be connected and the septic system properly abandoned under a permit.

Before any line cleaning, find out which kind of system your home uses. Hydro jetting a house line is not the same as servicing a septic tank or its leach field.

Coal country and glacial soil

Coal was mined throughout the township, and mining was the area's largest business for nearly 50 years (Main Street Wadsworth history). The county itself is covered by glacial till, lake deposits and outwash over bedrock, according to the ODNR groundwater pollution potential report for Medina County.

Soils like these hold water differently from place to place. That can matter for septic fields and for how long a basement stays wet after rain.

If you are on county sewer

The Medina County Sanitary Engineer says that after a backup, its staff can check the main during business hours and help find cleanouts and the length of the lateral. It suggests a plumber be ready to clear the full lateral from the house to the main.

rittman.heroP: Rittman sits where Wayne and Medina counties meet and was named for a railroad treasurer. It has its own water and sewer utility.

sections.html:
A railroad town with its own utilities

The City of Rittman says its first settlers took title to land in 1814 and that the town was named after the treasurer of the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad, whose line came through in the 1870s (Rittman history). Early businesses included grist mills, tile-making, wagon-building and tobacco farming.

The city lists water and sewer on its own utilities page, so questions about the public sewer go there rather than to Wadsworth.

What this means for your drain

A house near the old railroad stops or the square may be well over a century old. A clay tile line from the early days can sit next to a newer plastic section after a repair. Camera inspection shows the mix.

Because Rittman straddles two counties, check which office handles a given property before assuming who to call about permits or septic records.

sections.html:
A village on high ground

William Doyle laid out the village with 40 lots in 1827, and the village was incorporated in 1867 (Wikipedia on Doylestown, Wayne County Public Library wiki). The surrounding township was known as the great coal township of the county in an 1878 history (Wayne County history).

A hilltop village drains differently from a river flat. Water runs off the slope, so heavy rain tends to move downhill to the lower streets.

Village utilities

The village runs a Water/Sewer Department and says residents and businesses are served through it (Doylestown Water/Sewer Department). For a backup in the public system, start with the village.

For a slow drain inside a house, a camera inspection shows what is in the private line.

privacy.desc: Privacy policy for Wadsworth Hydro Jetting Pros: what request information is collected and how it is used.
privacy.heroP: This page explains what information this website collects and how it is used.

sections.html:
Information you send us

When you submit the request form we receive the name, phone number, email address and description of your drain problem that you enter. We use it to respond to your request and to connect you with a service provider who may be able to help.

Calls and analytics

This site uses Google Analytics and a call and form tracking script to understand how visitors use the pages and to attribute calls and requests. These tools may set cookies and collect technical data such as device type and pages visited.

Sharing

We may share your request details with service providers so they can contact you. We do not sell your information. We may disclose information if the law requires it.

Your choices
